entries.rationale: BEH-1 plus acceptance criterion 1 give exact assertions and counts; a one-glob YAML edit in templates/review-specs/defaults.yaml with a new test suite. Only wrinkle is a live-repo count (18 of 55) the plan already tells the author to pin with a comment.

Five files across lib/governance, skills/review-specs and two provider mirrors. Prompt wording must reconcile with 22j's provenance rule and name read tools derived from the resolved profile rather than hardcoded; prompt-safety phrasing is judgement work.

Scores 16/20 (auto band), held at assisted because review-config.mjs is a sensitive path and the plan flags a real error-ordering hazard around mergePacks. checkReadOnlyCompatible is a direct in-file precedent and option 1 is prescribed.

BEH-8 is written against a dispatch record that does not exist in the tree, so the planner had to invent where the behavior lives. Five files including two provider mirrors, a byte-stability constraint on renderReviewReport, and an explicit stop-and-escalate if a new lifecycle artifact seems needed.

Three-line edit with no backing behavior that changes what actually dispatches for every future review in this repo, and it collides with commit 863e119b on branch worktree-j7pq-review-gate. Transitively behind Task 8's gate. Needs a human to resolve the collision.

Prose only in docs/governance.md, extending an existing context-pack section, with five explicitly enumerated content requirements including the Known limitations note naming adev-plugin-j7pq.7 and both open gaps.

Scores 16/20 (auto band), held at assisted because context-pack.mjs is declared sensitive in governance/sensitive-paths.yaml and this is the head of the spine seven tasks depend on. Implementation is a direct copy of the max_file_bytes precedence loop.
Test-only parity guard, no production change expected, full assertion set and the denonce approach specified. Rev-4 context-pack.test.mjs is the oracle. Zero production files touched.

Rewrites both passes of renderPack, the shared surface behind reviewer dispatch AND three constitution-compliance checks in validate.yaml, under a byte-identity requirement for inline. Eight design constraints, one of which (SA-2) deliberately enforces nothing. Checkpoint after RED.

Security-sensitive and knowingly half-specified: SEC-1 is deferred to adev-plugin-j7pq.7, acceptance criterion 6 cannot be marked done, and the gap must be encoded as an executable assertion the plan describes only in prose. Human review of the boundary is warranted.

BEH-11's central claim (a denied path is never named) is explicitly not entailed pending SEC-2/j7pq.7. 22p-bis gives strong assertion precedent, but whether a production fix is needed is left to discovery and the author must consciously not close a known hole.

Spans two sensitive lib/governance modules and adds a new seam (dispatch-shape reading renderPack's budgets) serving all three dispatch stages. Implements SA-1's second recommendation, so the code intentionally diverges from BEH-12's current wording.

Gate-driven override above the 14/20 band. The edit is two trivial YAML lines, but it is the switch that exposes every reviewer to manifest delivery while SEC-1 and SEC-2 remain open in adev-plugin-j7pq.7. Judging that the gate has cleared is a human release decision, not an agent one.

Test-only, but the RED must be captured before Task 8 flips the bundled packs via a two-branch baseline procedure the author must choose and record. Also substitutes a measurable invariant for acceptance criterion 11, whose literal wording the plan admits is false.
